You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, Prisma/Postgres, separate worker/ process for provisioning jobs). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/**; API under app/api/**; business logic in lib/**; schema in prisma/schema.prisma.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do NOT run any command against the live database or live infrastructure. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-04-vps-capabilities.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED. The purpose is the 'nothing gets lost' safety net: every backend capability the VPS UI exposes must be listed so the redesign preserves it.

YOUR AUDIT: VPS / SERVER CAPABILITY INVENTORY (app/dashboard/servers/**, the server control panel, related components, API routes, worker jobs).
Produce:
1. Data model: the Prisma models behind VPS servers (Server/Vps/Instance/Plan/Region/Node/Snapshot/Backup/SshKey/Firewall/IpAddress/Activity/etc.) with the fields that the UI shows; the status enum(s) and their meaning; lifecycle transitions.
2. CAPABILITY TABLE: every user action available on a VPS, one row each: action name | where in UI (file + tab/section) | API route or server action | backend function (lib/...) | what it does on infra (Proxmox? which API) | confirmation/danger level | current UI state handling (loading/success/error) | reversible? | notes. Cover at minimum: list/filter/search servers, create/deploy, start, stop, shutdown, reboot, force reset, reinstall/rebuild (OS list), resize/upgrade/downgrade plan (which dims), rename, hostname, tags/labels, console/VNC/noVNC/web terminal, SSH keys (add/remove/attach), root password reset, rescue mode, snapshots (create/restore/delete, limits, pricing), backups (schedule/on-demand/restore/retention/pricing), files/SFTP/file manager, firewall/security groups (rules), networking (IPv4/IPv6/additional IPs/rDNS/private network/bandwidth), monitoring/metrics (which metrics, ranges, data source, refresh), activity/audit log, alerts, one-click apps/app installer (full app catalog list with source file), cloud-init/user-data, DNS quick-link, migration in/out, delete/destroy (with what's lost), billing links (upgrade, renew, cancel), transfer to team member, any 'control panel' features (cPanel-style panel from memory: what exists), any 'server directory' / public listing, health checks, ISO mount, boot order, kernel, any 'matrix' feature. Also any AI/agent features attached to servers (claude-code? build?).
3. Plans & regions: source of truth for VPS plans (file/db), each plan's specs and prices (monthly/yearly, currency handling), regions/datacenters available, stock/availability logic, promo/first-month-free logic that affects VPS.
4. Provisioning pipeline: exactly what happens after payment for a VPS (worker job chain, each step, the status/progress fields written to DB, what the client can poll/subscribe to — endpoints, intervals, SSE?), typical durations if logged/commented, failure modes and how they surface. This is needed for a TRUTHFUL deployment timeline UI: list the real states the UI can honestly display.
5. Which config values are REQUIRED at purchase (affect price/capacity/region/eligibility) vs can be changed AFTER provisioning via existing APIs (OS reinstall, hostname, SSH keys, firewall, backups, apps). For each post-provision-changeable item, cite the API that changes it.
6. Console/terminal/file-manager implementation details (libraries: xterm? noVNC? custom), because the redesign must preserve them.
7. Metrics implementation: data source, endpoints, chart library, ranges.
8. Team/permission gating on server actions (roles).
9. Gaps: capabilities present in backend but not exposed in UI, and UI controls that are stubs/no-ops.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~10-line summary (count of distinct capabilities, provisioning states, notable gaps).

527	async function stageAppFiles(conn: Client, recipe: Recipe, docRoot: string, appName: string): Promise<string> {
528	  assertPath(docRoot);
529	  assert(/^[a-z0-9._-]*$/.test(recipe.top), `Unsupported archive layout: ${recipe.top}`);
530	  assert(/^[a-z0-9._/-]+$/.test(recipe.marker), `Unsupported payload marker: ${recipe.marker}`);
531	  if (recipe.archive === "zip") await ensureUnzip(conn);
532	
533	  const top = recipe.top ? `${recipe.top}/` : "";
534	  const extract = recipe.archive === "zip" ? `unzip -q "$a" -d "$t/x"` : `tar -xzf "$a" -C "$t/x"`;
535	  const urls = recipe.sources.map(shellQuote).join(" ");
536	  const dest = shellQuote(docRoot);
537	
538	  const r = await exec(
539	    conn,
540	    `set -e; t=$(mktemp -d); a="$t/pkg"; mkdir -p "$t/x"; ok=""; ` +
541	      `for u in ${urls}; do if curl -fsSL --max-time 600 -o "$a" "$u"; then ok="$u"; break; fi; done; ` +
542	      `if [ -z "$ok" ]; then rm -rf "$t"; echo "NXAPP:NODOWNLOAD" >&2; exit 20; fi; ` +
543	      `if ! ${extract}; then rm -rf "$t"; echo "NXAPP:BADARCHIVE" >&2; exit 21; fi; ` +
544	      `if [ ! -e "$t/x/${top}${recipe.marker}" ]; then rm -rf "$t"; echo "NXAPP:BADPAYLOAD" >&2; exit 22; fi; ` +
545	      `mkdir -p ${dest}; cp -a "$t/x/${top}." ${dest}/; rm -rf "$t"; ` +
546	      `printf 'NXAPP:FROM %s\\n' "$ok"`,
547	    INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS
548	  );
549	  const out = `${r.stdout}\n${r.stderr}`;
550	  if (/NXAPP:NODOWNLOAD/.test(out))
551	    throw new Error(`could not download ${appName} from any known release URL — nothing was changed on the server.`);
552	  if (/NXAPP:BADARCHIVE/.test(out)) throw new Error(`the ${appName} download was not a readable archive.`);
553	  if (/NXAPP:BADPAYLOAD/.test(out))
554	    throw new Error(`the ${appName} download did not contain ${recipe.marker} — refusing to treat it as ${appName}.`);

558	  // Prove the files landed where nginx will look, rather than trusting cp -a.

593	 * the customer was shown actually exists.

596	 *  - it defined ONE weak AUTH_KEY, so every site shared guessable cookie salts;

621	  assertInertSecret(admin.password, "admin password");
622	
623	  const salts = WP_SALT_KEYS.map((k) => `define('${k}', '${rand()}');`).join("\n");
624	  const cfg =
625	    `<?php\n` +
626	    `/* Generated by the Nxeon control panel — one-click WordPress install. */\n` +
627	    `define('DB_NAME', '${creds.name}');\n` +
628	    `define('DB_USER', '${creds.user}');\n` +
629	    `define('DB_PASSWORD', '${creds.password}');\n` +
630	    `define('DB_HOST', 'localhost');\n` +
631	    `define('DB_CHARSET', 'utf8mb4');\n` +
632	    `define('DB_COLLATE', '');\n` +
633	    `${salts}\n` +
634	    `define('WP_DEBUG', false);\n` +
635	    // Deliberately NOT defining WP_HOME/WP_SITEURL: hardcoding http:// here
636	    // would grey out Settings → General and strand the customer on http after
637	    // they enable SSL from this panel. The installer seeds the URL options
638	    // instead, so WordPress can be moved to https from its own admin.
639	    `$table_prefix = 'wp_';\n` +
640	    `if ( ! defined('ABSPATH') ) define('ABSPATH', __DIR__ . '/');\n` +
641	    `require_once ABSPATH . 'wp-settings.php';\n`;
642	  const wrote = await execInput(
643	    conn,
644	    `umask 037; cat > ${shellQuote(`${docRoot}/wp-config.php`)}`,
645	    cfg,
646	    SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS
647	  );
648	  if (wrote.code !== 0) throw new Error(`could not write wp-config.php: ${why(wrote)}`);
649	
650	  const script =
651	    `<?php\n` +
652	    `/* Nxeon one-click WordPress finish — run once, then deleted. */\n` +
653	    `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'] = ${php(domain)};\n` +
654	    `$_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'] = ${php(domain)};\n` +
655	    `$_SERVER['SERVER_PORT'] = '80';\n` +
656	    `$_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] = '/';\n` +
657	    `$_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'] = '/index.php';\n` +
658	    `$_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] = 'GET';\n` +
659	    // wp_guess_url() honours WP_SITEURL, so the siteurl/home options are seeded
660	    // with the real domain instead of a CLI-derived guess.
661	    `define('WP_SITEURL', ${php(`http://${domain}`)});\n` +
662	    `define('WP_HOME', ${php(`http://${domain}`)});\n` +
663	    `define('WP_INSTALLING', true);\n` +
664	    `require_once ${php(`${docRoot}/wp-load.php`)};\n` +
665	    `require_once ABSPATH . 'wp-admin/includes/upgrade.php';\n` +
666	    `if ( is_blog_installed() ) { fwrite(STDERR, "NXWP:ALREADY\\n"); exit(31); }\n` +
667	    `$res = wp_install(${php(domain)}, ${php(admin.user)}, ${php(admin.email)}, true, '', ${php(admin.password)});\n` +
668	    `if ( is_wp_error($res) ) { fwrite(STDERR, 'NXWP:ERR ' . $res->get_error_message() . "\\n"); exit(32); }\n` +
669	    `$uid = ( is_array($res) && isset($res['user_id']) ) ? $res['user_id'] : 0;\n` +
670	    `if ( is_wp_error($uid) || (int) $uid < 1 ) { fwrite(STDERR, "NXWP:NOUSER\\n"); exit(33); }\n` +
671	    `$u = get_user_by('login', ${php(admin.user)});\n` +
672	    `if ( ! $u || (int) $u->ID !== (int) $uid ) { fwrite(STDERR, "NXWP:NOACCOUNT\\n"); exit(34); }\n` +
673	    // The whole point: prove the password we are about to show authenticates.
674	    `if ( ! wp_check_password(${php(admin.password)}, $u->user_pass, $u->ID) ) { fwrite(STDERR, "NXWP:BADPASS\\n"); exit(35); }\n` +
675	    `if ( ! in_array('administrator', (array) $u->roles, true) ) { fwrite(STDERR, "NXWP:NOTADMIN\\n"); exit(36); }\n` +
676	    `echo "NXWP:OK user=" . (int) $u->ID . "\\n";\n`;

678	  const run = await execInput(
679	    conn,
680	    `umask 077; f=$(mktemp) && cat > "$f" && ` +
681	      `p=$(command -v php${phpVersion} 2>/dev/null || command -v php 2>/dev/null); ` +
